outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the statement has been claimed false for infinitely many r by an OpenAI release (preprints dated 23 and 27 September 2026; Lean-stated; no independent mathematician's check found), while P. White (13 September 2026, unreviewed) claims the (r,ν)=(4,2) case and an open Lean repository (3 October 2026) claims (4,3).
problem_asks: Reading of the bullet 'Ryser's conjecture relating the maximum matching size and the minimum transversal size in hypergraphs' in its standard form, which the frozen statement does not spell out (r-partiteness is supplied from the literature): for every integer r ≥ 2 and every r-partite r-uniform hypergraph H, τ(H) ≤ (r−1)·ν(H), where τ(H) is the minimum vertex-cover (transversal) size and ν(H) the maximum matching size. Parts: (a) the inequality for each r ≥ 2; (b) for each such H, the inequality at its own ν(H); (c) the universal claim that (a) and (b) hold for all r at once. Without r-partiteness the inequality τ ≤ r·ν is already known, so the conjecture is the one-step reduction of the factor. The statement does not name intersecting hypergraphs, sharpness, or any particular (r,ν); those are cases of it.

events.what_happened: Kőnig's theorem: for bipartite graphs (the r=2 case) the transversal number equals the matching number, so τ ≤ (r−1)ν holds with r=2. Cited as the r=2 case in the Formal Conjectures database (PR #6812: 'r = 2 (Kőnig 1931)') and in Wikipedia's account of the known cases.
events.delivers: The r=2 instance in full: τ(H) = ν(H) for every 2-partite 2-uniform hypergraph, i.e. every bipartite graph.
events.remains: Every r ≥ 3: r=3 (settled by aharoni-2001-r3) and every r ≥ 4.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound at r=2.
people: Kőnig (first name not given in the sources read)

events.what_happened: Tuza's 1979 manuscript listed the case (r,ν)=(4,2), namely τ ≤ 6, among his solved cases of the conjecture, with no proof given. DeBiasio, Kamel, McCourt and Sheats (arXiv:2009.07239, 2020) record it in §3 as 'the case (r,α)=(4,2) is claimed in [57] and [58], but no proof is given', using the graph-colouring notation with α. Their list of proved cases, (r,α) in {(3,1),(3,2),(3,3),(3,4),(4,1),(5,1)}, omits (4,2). White (2026) and the Formal Conjectures PR cite it as Tuza (1979, 1983).
events.revisions: 1979 manuscript (no public copy found); 1983 publication in Ars Combinatoria 16B, 201-209, per White's reference list (not opened).
events.delivers: Nothing. It names the (4,2) case and asserts the bound there, without a proof.
events.doubts: Claimed without proof in both sources read (the 2020 survey §3; White's introduction). White's acknowledgements thank the survey authors 'for recording Tuza's claim precisely enough to make the gap visible', so the gap was identified before the 2026 proof.
events.direction: Asserts the conjectured bound at (4,2), without proof.

events.what_happened: Tuza's intersecting-case results (ν=1) for r=4 and r=5. DeBiasio et al. (2020, §1) credit 'r=4 and ν=1 by Tuza [57]' and 'r=5 and ν=1 by Tuza [57]', with the (4,1) proof in [57] and [59]. The Formal Conjectures PR table credits r=4, ν=1 to 'Gyárfás 1977; Tuza 1979, 1994' and r=5, ν=1 to 'Tuza 1979'. White's introduction credits Gyárfás for r=3,4 and Tuza for r=5 in the intersecting case.
events.revisions: Year given as 1978 (Wikipedia text), 1979 (PR; White), 1983 (Ars Combinatoria listing) and 1994 (PR, for r=4). 1979 is used here; the others are in disputes.
events.delivers: The intersecting case (any two edges meet, so ν=1) for r=4, giving τ ≤ 3, and for r=5, giving τ ≤ 4.
events.remains: Intersecting hypergraphs with r ≥ 6 in general (the linear intersecting subcase for r ≤ 9 is covered by francetic-et-al-2015-linear-intersecting); every ν ≥ 2 at r ≥ 4 not settled by another event.
events.doubts: The 2020 survey disagrees with itself: §1 credits the r=5, ν=1 case to Tuza [57], while §3 says 'since the r=5 case is unpublished'. The attribution to Gyárfás appears only in the PR table, not in the survey text read.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound in the intersecting case at r=4 and r=5.

events.what_happened: Aharoni, 'Ryser's conjecture for tripartite 3-graphs', Combinatorica 21 (2001) 1-4, proves the case r=3: τ ≤ 2ν for every 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph, by topological methods (Wikipedia credits the Aharoni–Haxell Hall-type theorem). The citation is confirmed in the reference lists of White and of the Formal Conjectures PR. The article itself was not read: its Springer page redirected to a login page.
events.revisions: Journal publication 2001. A search snippet gives 'received March 17, 1999' and a dissertation snippet says 'In 1999, Aharoni gave a proof'. If an earlier written argument exists it was not located, so the year given is the journal year.
events.delivers: The r=3 case in full: τ(H) ≤ 2ν(H) for every 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph, for all ν.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2001 (publication record as cited by White and the Formal Conjectures PR; the article was not opened)

events.direction: Confirms the conjectured bound at r=3.

events.what_happened: Haxell and Scott, 'On Ryser's conjecture', Electronic J. Combin. 19(1) (2012) #P23, published 21 Jan 2012 (DOI 10.37236/1175). Proves that for r=4 and r=5 there is ε>0 such that every r-partite r-uniform hypergraph H has a cover of size at most (r−ε)ν(H). The abstract gives no value of ε. White states that this gives τ ≤ 7 at (r,ν)=(4,2), the previous best bound.
events.revisions: Journal publication 21 Jan 2012. An earlier preprint was not checked.
events.delivers: For r=4 and r=5, all ν: τ ≤ (r−ε)ν for an unspecified ε>0. This reduces the factor r by some ε; it does not reach r−1.
events.remains: The exact factor r−1 for r=4 and r=5 at each ν not settled by another event, and every r ≥ 6.

checked_by.who: The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics (journal of record)

events.direction: Partial, in the conjectured direction: reduces the factor r to r−ε at r=4 and r=5, weaker than r−1.

events.what_happened: Francetić, Herke, McKay and Wanless, 'On Ryser's conjecture for linear intersecting multipartite hypergraphs', arXiv:1508.00951 (v1 5 Aug 2015; v2 28 Sep 2015; v3 29 Sep 2015), Eur. J. Combin. 61 (2017) 91-105. Proves τ ≤ (r−1)ν for r ≤ 9 in the special case of linear intersecting hypergraphs (every two edges meet in exactly one vertex). Also gives a counterexample to Aharoni's stronger form (a cover of a particular shape) at r=13, ν=1; shows no linear intersecting example attains τ=r−1 at r=7; reports computational results.
events.revisions: v1 5 Aug 2015; v2 28 Sep 2015; v3 29 Sep 2015 (current). Journal: Eur. J. Combin. 61 (2017) 91-105.
events.delivers: Restricted case: τ ≤ (r−1)ν for 4 ≤ r ≤ 9 when H is intersecting and linear (every two edges share exactly one vertex). Intersecting implies ν=1. Separately, a counterexample to Aharoni's stronger version at r=13, ν=1, which is not Ryser's statement.
events.remains: Intersecting hypergraphs with r = 6 to 9 that are not linear; all intersecting H with r ≥ 10; every ν ≥ 2 at r ≥ 4 not covered by another event.

checked_by.who: European Journal of Combinatorics (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published vol. 61 (2017) pp. 91-105 (journal reference shown on the arXiv page)

events.directly_checkable: Explicit finite hypergraphs are claimed (linear intersecting examples; non-linear examples at r in {9,13,17}); I did not check them.
events.direction: Confirms the bound for linear intersecting hypergraphs with r ≤ 9. The counterexample is to Aharoni's stronger form, not to Ryser's bound.
events.object: Explicit linear intersecting hypergraphs at r=7 and r=8 in the stated classes, non-linear intersecting examples attaining τ=r−1 at r in {9,13,17}, and a counterexample to Aharoni's stronger conjecture at r=13, ν=1. The abstract does not describe the objects beyond these statements.

events.what_happened: Haxell and Scott, 'A note on intersecting hypergraphs with large cover number', arXiv:1609.05458 (v1 18 Sep 2016; v2 6 Oct 2017). Constructs r-partite r-uniform intersecting hypergraphs with cover number at least r−4 for all but finitely many r, answering a question of Abu-Khazneh, Barát, Pokrovskiy and Szabó. The abstract says this shows Ryser's conjecture 'is close to being best possible for every value of r'.
events.revisions: v1 18 Sep 2016; v2 6 Oct 2017. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: A lower-bound construction: for all but finitely many r, an intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraph with τ ≥ r−4 (so ν=1 and τ within 3 of the conjectured r−1). It does not reach r−1, so it decides no upper bound.
events.remains: The upper bound τ ≤ (r−1)ν is not decided by this; the gap between r−4 and r−1 remains in the intersecting case.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjectured bound: a lower-bound construction that stays below r−1.
events.object: Intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraphs with cover number at least r−4, for all but finitely many r. The abstract states the construction without describing it.

events.what_happened: Keevash, Pokrovskiy, Sudakov and Yepremyan, 'New bounds for Ryser's conjecture and related problems', arXiv:2005.00526 (v1 1 May 2020; v2 25 May 2020). Gives Latin square transversals of order n−O(log n/log log n) (the Ryser–Brualdi–Stein problem), plus Steiner triple system and Latin array results. The abstract does not mention r-partite hypergraphs.
events.delivers: Nothing for the hypergraph statement. This is a result on a different problem (transversals of Latin squares) that carries the name 'Ryser's conjecture' in the literature.

events.what_happened: Gyárfás and Sárközy, 'Bounded diameter variations of Ryser's conjecture', arXiv:2505.02564 (v1 5 May 2025; no later version listed). For a graph with α(G)=2 and any 2-colouring of its edges, V(G) can be covered by two monochromatic subgraphs of diameter at most 4, improving DeBiasio et al. For diameter 2 and 2 ≤ r ≤ 3 the exact answer is rα; for diameter 4 and r=2 the bound is ⌊3α/2⌋. Asks whether diameter 4 can be reduced to 3. Pith (an AI referee platform) reviewed the paper on 16 Aug 2026.
events.revisions: v1 5 May 2025; no later version listed.
events.delivers: Bounded-diameter monochromatic component covers for edge-coloured graphs with α=2 (diameter 4), exact values for diameter 2 with r in {2,3}, and a diameter-4 bound for r=2. A variant of the coloured-graph form of Ryser's statement, not the hypergraph bound.
events.remains: The hypergraph bound τ ≤ (r−1)ν; the diameter-3 question; the coloured-graph statement for general α and r.

checked_by.qualification: none: an automated AI referee. The page itself says the review is machine-generated and that no human expert has reviewed the paper yet.
checked_by.what_they_did: Review dated 16 Aug 2026; verdict 'worth refereeing, with only minor cleanup needed'; five minor objections, the most substantive about applying Proposition 3.1 to diameter-3 starting graphs

events.direction: No direction on the hypergraph bound. For the coloured-graph variant it proves bounded-diameter covers with diameter 4 when α=2.

events.what_happened: Clow, Haxell and Mohar, 'A counterexample to a conjecture of Lovász', arXiv:2505.05339 (v1 8 May 2025; v2 10 Jun 2025). Lovász's 1975 conjecture: every r-partite r-uniform H has r−1 vertices whose deletion lowers the matching number. The abstract says this would imply a well-known 1971 conjecture of Ryser. The authors show it false for r=3, using the line hypergraph of the Biggs–Smith graph (a cubic graph on 102 vertices).
events.delivers: Lovász's stronger deletion conjecture is false for r=3. Restriction: r=3 only. It does not decide Ryser's bound.
events.remains: Ryser's conjecture in full (its r−1 bound at all r and ν); Lovász's conjecture for r ≥ 4.
events.directly_checkable: The counterexample is an explicit graph (Biggs–Smith) and its line hypergraph, named in the abstract. I did not check the deletion property by hand.
events.direction: Counterexample to a stronger, sufficient-condition conjecture of Lovász. The abstract says Lovász's statement would imply Ryser's, so this failure does not by itself refute Ryser's bound.
events.object: The line hypergraph of the Biggs–Smith graph, a cubic graph on 102 vertices: an explicit 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph for which no two-vertex deletion lowers the matching number.

events.what_happened: Abiad, Garbe, Povill and Spiegel, 'Infinitely many counterexamples to a conjecture of Lovász', arXiv:2506.21286 (v1 26 Jun 2025; v2 14 Jul 2025). Builds on Clow, Haxell and Mohar: a simple infinite family of r=3 counterexamples to Lovász's conjecture based on generalized Petersen graphs, and specific counterexamples for r=4. The abstract describes Lovász's conjecture as a stronger conjecture motivated by Ryser's.
events.delivers: Infinitely many r=3 counterexamples and specific r=4 counterexamples to Lovász's deletion conjecture. Restriction: this is a stronger statement than Ryser's and the abstract makes no claim about the hypergraph bound.
events.remains: Ryser's conjecture in full. The abstract does not address Lovász's conjecture for r ≥ 5.
events.direction: Counterexamples to Lovász's stronger conjecture, not to Ryser's bound.
events.object: An infinite family of 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraphs built from generalized Petersen graphs, and specific 4-partite counterexamples. The abstract names the family but I did not read the construction.

events.what_happened: Pokrovskiy, 'Bounded diameter monochromatic component covers', arXiv:2507.05842 (v1 8 Jul 2025; v2 6 Jan 2026). States Ryser's coloured-complete-graph statement (every r-edge-coloured complete graph can be covered by r−1 monochromatic trees) and Milićević's stronger bounded-diameter version, and shows the two are equivalent. As corollaries, Milićević's conjecture holds for r=5 and several cases of a DeBiasio–Kamel–McCourt–Sheats generalisation to non-complete graphs follow. The abstract does not mention hypergraphs.
events.revisions: v1 8 Jul 2025 (abstract says 'trees'); v2 6 Jan 2026 (says 'components' in the published-style wording, per a search summary). A DOI 10.1112/mtk.70123 appears in a search snippet; the journal version was not verified.
events.delivers: Equivalence of the coloured-complete-graph covering statement with its bounded-diameter form; Milićević's conjecture holds for r=5; new cases of the non-complete-graph generalisation. Restriction: statements about edge-coloured graphs, not τ and ν of hypergraphs.
events.remains: The hypergraph bound τ ≤ (r−1)ν, which the paper does not address as read. Whether the coloured-graph statement is equivalent to the hypergraph conjecture is not established in the sources read; the 2020 survey gives a graph-colouring restatement, but its full text was not readable here.
events.doubts: The journal version and any refereeing were not located; the paper's full text was not read, only the abstract page.
events.direction: No direction on the hypergraph bound. For the coloured-graph covering statement, it establishes equivalence with a bounded-diameter form and proves that form for r=5.

events.what_happened: Hawranick and Luo, 'Covering complete r-partite r-uniform hypergraphs with few monochromatic components', arXiv:2603.04704 (submitted 5 Mar 2026, math.CO). For k ≥ 2r ≥ 6, in every spanning k-edge-colouring of a complete r-partite r-uniform hypergraph the vertices can be covered by at most k−r+1 monochromatic components. The authors say this proves a conjecture of Gyárfás and Király 'which is related to a special case of Ryser's conjecture'. They also treat k ∈ {2,3} for complete bipartite graphs.
events.delivers: A covering bound by k−r+1 monochromatic components for k ≥ 2r ≥ 6 spanning colourings of complete r-partite r-uniform hypergraphs. The authors describe it as related to a special case of Ryser's conjecture. The abstract does not state the τ and ν bound.
events.remains: The bound τ ≤ (r−1)ν. The abstract does not identify the special case, so the relation is the authors' description and is not established here.
events.doubts: The link to Ryser's conjecture is stated only as 'related to a special case'; the special case is not named in the abstract read.
events.direction: No direction on the Ryser bound stated in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Patrick White (single author, independent researcher, no affiliation shown) posted arXiv:2609.14281, 'Tuza's Ryser-conjecture claim for four-partite hypergraphs with matching number two', about 5 pages. Claims every 4-partite 4-uniform hypergraph H with ν(H)=2 satisfies τ(H) ≤ 6, confirming Tuza's 1979 claim that had no proof. The argument combines Gyárfás's theorem for intersecting 4-partite 4-uniform families (τ ≤ 3), a projection lemma (Lemma 2.2), and König's matching theorem. Per the paper's Methods, the projection lemma and the five-sentence proof were found by GPT-5.6 Sol (see ai).
events.revisions: v1 13 Sep 2026 only. arXiv:2609.14281v2 returned HTTP 404 when checked on 13 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: The (r,ν)=(4,2) instance of τ(H) ≤ (r−1)ν(H): every 4-partite 4-uniform H with ν(H)=2 has τ(H) ≤ 6. Restrictions: r=4, 4-uniform, and ν exactly 2. Nothing is stated for other ν or other r.
events.remains: Still open after this event: r=4 with ν ≥ 4; r=5 with ν ≥ 2; every r ≥ 6; and the conjecture for all r at once. (r=4 with ν=3 is claimed by kitamura-2026-r4-nu3-lean; r=4 and r=5 with ν=1 by earlier work.)
events.directly_checkable: A roughly 5-page argument using Gyárfás's intersecting theorem, the paper's projection lemma (Lemma 2.2), and König's theorem. The Methods say the model's structural claims were checked by exact computation (MILP via scipy.optimize.milp and brute-force enumeration). No object is exhibited. The computations are not described in the text I read beyond that.
events.doubts: No specific error identified and no published critique found through 13 Oct 2026. Signals: a single author with no affiliation shown; a key lemma that the author attributes to an AI system (Methods); no journal or referee; the AI-first tracker VibeMathed (checked 22 Sep 2026) records 'Verification: Unreviewed' and says 'The mathematics was not checked here'; MathWorld reports that as of 22 Sep 2026 no independent specialist review had been reported. Statement: the abstract and Theorem 1.1 read τ(H) ≤ 6 in the HTML extraction. A strict τ(H) < 6 appears only in a search summary of a PDF extraction, which I could not read directly; I treat it as an extraction artefact, unconfirmed. Search summaries also report that the author found two corrections to the model's intermediate claims; that is not in the text I read.
events.direction: Cuts in the direction the conjecture predicts: confirms the bound τ ≤ (r−1)ν at (r,ν)=(4,2).

systems.name: GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI, model gpt-5.6-sol-pro)
systems.what_it_did: Per the paper's Methods: the proof was 'found through four rounds of structured reasoning', each round building on verified output of the previous one. Round 4 found the projection lemma (Lemma 2.2) and the five-sentence proof, bypassing the entire apparatus of rounds 2-3. The author states that every structural claim returned by the model was independently verified by his own exact computation (MILP via scipy.optimize.milp, and brute-force enumeration) before incorporation. The authors credit this system with the lemma the proof turns on.
systems.basis_quote: Round 4 found the projection lemma (Lemma 2.2) and the five-sentence proof above, bypassing the entire apparatus of rounds 2–3.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math repository (a single root commit, 'Initial commit', adc7f12, author shown as 'Anonymous') documents in lean/docs/162.md 'Counterexamples to Ryser's covering conjecture' and links the preprint 'A Counterexample to Ryser's Covering Conjecture', dated 23 Sep 2026 by its file path. Its Lean files are in lean/ComparatorChallenges/ (RyserCovering.lean, RyserOddExtensions.lean). Claims: (i) for a fixed prime p ≡ 2 (mod 3), p > 5, and all sufficiently large prime n, there is an intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraph with r = p^n+1, matching number 1 and cover number r, so τ > (r−1)ν; (ii) for every sufficiently large prime p ≡ 2 (mod 3) and every sufficiently large odd n (threshold depending on p), the same failure holds at r = p^n+1, and the set of such ranks is infinite. The formal catalogue lists the entry with authors 'OpenAI'. The release was reported on 6 Oct 2026 by secondary coverage; the 23 Sep date comes from the file path, not from a posting record.
events.revisions: Single commit adc7f12 with no date shown. Preprint date taken from the file path. Release reported 6 Oct 2026. No arXiv listing found. Release-level corrections are reported (three manuscripts withdrawn, fourteen revised); the sources read do not say whether any Ryser manuscript was affected.
events.delivers: If correct: for each rank r = p^n+1 in the stated families, an intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraph with ν=1 and τ=r, which violates τ ≤ (r−1)ν at that r. The Lean definition CounterexampleRank r requires 0 < r, a nonempty H, RPartiteUniform r H (a part map V → Fin r), Intersecting H (distinct edges meet), a cover, matchingNumber H = 1 and coverNumber H = r. Restrictions: ν=1; ranks of the stated shapes only; thresholds not explicit; no claim for r ≤ 5 (VibeMathed quotes the release as saying the small cases remain open).
events.remains: Every r not of the stated forms, including the whole range r ≤ 5 and the other ranks at r ≥ 6; the bound for non-intersecting H; and every (r,ν) with ν ≥ 2 except as other events state. If the claims hold, the bound fails at the listed ranks only.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 weeks from 23 Sep (1 week from the 6 Oct release)

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib. Comparator challenge files (contain sorry by design). Solution modules named in the comparator configs (OAI/Combinatorics/Ryser/Construction/Main.lean and its four imports; OAI/Combinatorics/Ryser/OddExtensions.lean) read sorry-free through a model-mediated reading. I did not run Lean. The repo does not state a comparator run result.

events.directly_checkable: The statement is checkable by reading the Lean definitions (quoted in the summary). The release text gives no construction. The solution modules rely on finite-field extension lemmas (Field/ExtensionSubfields) and a gadget lemma named exists_prime_goodGadget, which suggests existence arguments. Whether the hypergraphs are explicit is not determined by me.
events.doubts: (1) The release says 'Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations' and that 'some of the unformalized results could have issues' (README). (2) The challenge files prove their main theorem with sorry; the solution modules were read but not rebuilt. VibeMathed records 'Lean-checked, statement unaudited'; the repo's 162.md says only that a formalization exists; Kalai calls even Lean verification into question (see disputes). (3) No written check by a mathematician was found. Kalai (7 Oct 2026) says the results 'will need to be verified and digested by human mathematicians in the months to come'. VibeMathed says 'No independent mathematician has checked this yet'. (4) The preprint PDFs could not be read, so the paper's own argument and caveats are unknown to me. (5) The claim is not in conflict with any earlier result read, since the ranks are large and the earlier positive results are for r ≤ 9 (linear intersecting) and r ≤ 5 (intersecting).
events.direction: Cuts against the conjectured bound. It claims intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraphs with ν=1 and τ=r, i.e. τ > (r−1)ν, at the listed ranks. The repo says the constructions 'contradict the bound τ ≤ (r−1)ν'. VibeMathed quotes the release as saying 'Ryser's conjecture is false, already for intersecting hypergraphs'.
events.object: Claimed: for each listed rank r = p^n+1, a finite intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraph H with matching number 1 and cover number r (a minimum cover has size r). In the Lean statement: a finite type V, a hypergraph H on V with a part map V → Fin r, distinct edges meeting, and cover number r. No explicit hypergraph is given in the sources read; whether the construction is explicit or existential is not determined by me.

systems.name: an unreleased internal OpenAI model
systems.what_it_did: The release README says: 'The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.' The Ryser entry (lean/docs/162.md) names no system and describes no procedure. The README's listed exceptions (a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not include Ryser. Attribution to this model is therefore release-level and inferred for this entry. The preprint text, which would carry a per-paper statement, could not be read.
systems.basis_quote: The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.

ai.disclosed_cost: README, release-wide and not per result: 'On average, each result used three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute with that model.' No monetary cost disclosed, and no Ryser-specific figure.

events.what_happened: Companion preprint 'Balanced Counterexamples to Ryser's Conjecture at Prime Orders', dated 27 Sep 2026 by its file path, in the same openai/math release. Its challenge file lean/ComparatorChallenges/BalancedRyser.lean states OAI.Balanced.main_result: there is q0 such that for every prime q ≥ q0, the predicate BalancedCounterexample q holds. The prose claim (lean/docs/162.md): for every sufficiently large prime q there is a finite intersecting (q+1)-partite, (q+1)-uniform hypergraph with cover number q+1 and exactly q+1 non-isolated vertices in each part, so the parts are equal and τ = q+1 > (r−1)ν with r = q+1, ν = 1. The solution module named in the comparator config (OAI.Combinatorics.BalancedRyser.Main) is an import-only file of 10 lines in what I read; the declaration was not located among the files read. The formal catalogue, as read, has no entry mentioning 'Balanced'.
events.revisions: Dated by file path (27 Sep 2026). Release reported 6 Oct 2026. No arXiv listing found.
events.delivers: If correct: for every prime q above an existential threshold, an intersecting (q+1)-partite (q+1)-uniform hypergraph with equal part sizes, ν=1 and τ=q+1, violating τ ≤ (r−1)ν at r=q+1. Restrictions: r = q+1 with q a large prime; equal parts; existential threshold.
events.remains: Every other rank, including every r below the threshold; the p^n+1 family is a different shape and is covered by its own event; every ν ≥ 2 at r ≥ 4 except as other events state.
events.time_since_posted: about 2.5 weeks from 27 Sep (1 week from the 6 Oct release)

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib. Comparator challenge main_result (contains sorry by design). Solution declaration not located in the files read.

events.directly_checkable: The object is a family of hypergraphs for each large prime q, with equal parts and cover number q+1. The release text gives no construction in the sources read, so I could not check it.
events.doubts: The same release-level doubts as openai-2026-p-power-plus-one-counterexample apply: no independent check found, release described as at 'different stages of verification', and the Ryser entry called a provisional counterexample by Kalai. In addition, the Lean declaration for the solution was not located, so the existence of a Lean proof for this companion is unverified.
events.direction: Cuts against the conjectured bound. It claims τ = q+1 > q = (r−1)ν for intersecting, equal-part r-partite hypergraphs with r = q+1.
events.object: Claimed: for every sufficiently large prime q, a finite intersecting (q+1)-partite (q+1)-uniform hypergraph with cover number q+1 and exactly q+1 non-isolated vertices in each part. The Lean predicate BalancedCounterexample q is not defined in the files read. Not explicit in the sources read.

events.what_happened: Repository KitaKen1/ryser-4partite-nu3 (Apache-2.0), created 3 Oct 2026 (GitHub created_at 2026-10-03T08:30:11Z), the same day as Formal Conjectures pull request #6812 by KitaKen1, 'Formalize Ryser's conjecture and mark r = 4, ν ≤ 3 as solved'. The PR is open and unmerged on 13 Oct 2026 ('awaiting-author' label added 8 Oct). The repo claims a Lean 4 proof that every finite 4-partite 4-uniform hypergraph H with ν(H)=3 satisfies τ(H) ≤ 9. The README gives the formal statement as τ(H) ≤ 3ν(H) for ν ≤ 3, leaves ν ≥ 4 for r=4 and most r ≥ 5 open, and credits the ν=2 case to White (arXiv:2609.14281), citing White's Lemma 2.2 as the projection argument used in its Lemma 2.
events.revisions: Repository created 3 Oct 2026, pushed the same day. PR #6812 opened 3 Oct 2026; 'awaiting-author' label added 8 Oct 2026 by a bot; the PR was still open on 13 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Claims the (r,ν)=(4,3) instance: τ ≤ 9 for every finite 4-partite 4-uniform H with ν=3. The formal statement is said to cover ν ≤ 3, and the README credits ν=1 and ν=2 to earlier work and to White. Restrictions: r=4, 4-uniform, finite H; the new content is ν=3.
events.remains: r=4 with ν ≥ 4 (README: open); r=5 with ν ≥ 2 and every r ≥ 6 (PR and README: open); the conjecture for all r at once.

events.directly_checkable: Finite case analysis certified by the Lean kernel. The README reports 39,794 nine-edge families reduced by isomorphisms to 2,436 representatives, each carrying a refutation, with certificates checked by decide +kernel and no native_decide. The reviewer counts 232 case obligations. The README's mathematical sketch is headed 'Mathematical explanation (AI generated)'.
events.doubts: (1) The proof is a finite case analysis; the reduction and the certificates are the claim, and neither has been rerun by anyone I found. (2) The reviewer's bridge check is conditional on Ryser.ryser_through_three and the 232 case obligations were not replayed. (3) The README attributes Lemma 2 to 'the projection argument of White (arXiv:2609.14281, Lemma 2.2)'. If the Lean chain uses it, this result depends on the unreviewed ν=2 lemma; I did not verify the dependency. (4) The PR is open and labelled 'awaiting-author'; the repo is 10 days old with no stars; no written review found. (5) The formal-conjectures entry is titled as marking the case solved while the PR is unmerged.
events.direction: Confirms the bound at (r,ν)=(4,3), with the claimed value τ ≤ 9 equal to (r−1)ν.

disputes.summary: Origin of the conjecture. Wikipedia credits first appearance to J. R. Henderson's 1971 PhD thesis under Ryser, and MathWorld gives the same. Pokrovskiy's abstract opens 'Ryser conjectured...'. A search summary reports Pokrovskiy saying it is unclear whether Ryser made the conjecture. Not resolved here; the thesis was not read.

Dates and credit for Tuza's results. The year of Tuza's claims is given as 1978 (Wikipedia text), 1979 (White; the Formal Conjectures PR), 1983 (Ars Combinatoria publication, per White's references) and 1994 (PR, for r=4, ν=1). The PR credits r=4, ν=1 to 'Gyárfás 1977; Tuza 1979, 1994', while White credits Gyárfás for r=3,4 and Tuza for r=5 in the intersecting case.
DeBiasio et al. (2020) disagree with themselves on the r=5, ν=1 case: §1 credits it to Tuza [57] as proved, while §3 says 'since the r=5 case is unpublished'.

White's paper names the model two ways. The arXiv comments field says 'Proof found via four rounds of GPT-5.6 Pro; AI assistance disclosed in Methods'. The Methods section says 'GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI, model gpt-5.6-sol-pro)'. MathWorld says 'GPT-5.6 Sol'. The Methods wording is recorded as the authors' account; the comments-field wording is noted.

Sources disagree on the Lean status of the OpenAI counterexamples. VibeMathed lists 'Lean-checked, statement unaudited'. The repo's lean/docs/162.md describes Lean formalizations and does not say whether they compile. The challenge files prove their main theorems with sorry, and the solution modules read sorry-free but were not rebuilt. Kalai says even Lean verification may have problems.

White's abstract and Theorem 1.1 read τ(H) ≤ 6 in the HTML extraction. A search summary of a PDF extraction reported τ(H) < 6. I recorded ≤, which the HTML read directly; the PDF was not readable through WebFetch.

Status of the conjecture at different dates. ProofAtlas (status checked 6 Aug 2026) lists it as open for every r ≥ 4. MathWorld and the Formal Conjectures PR (3 Oct 2026, open, unmerged) list the general conjecture as open and mark only r=4 cases as solved, and I did not see the OpenAI counterexamples mentioned in what I read of the PR. The OpenAI repo (Sep 2026) claims counterexamples for infinitely many r. These sources describe the same question at different dates and are not yet reconciled.

summary: I ran 44 search queries and opened about 50 pages and repository files; the protocol's minimum was 30. Three in-window claims touch the statement, each at a different status. (1) OpenAI's October 2026 release (openai/math, commit adc7f12; preprints dated 23 and 27 Sep 2026 by file path; reported 6 Oct) includes Lean-stated claims that the bound fails for intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraphs with ν=1 and τ=r at ranks r=p^n+1 (p ≡ 2 mod 3, p > 5, n large) and, in a companion, at r=q+1 for large primes q with equal parts. If correct, these falsify τ ≤ (r−1)ν at those ranks. Each challenge file proves its main theorem with sorry, which is the design of a comparator challenge. The solution modules named in the comparator configs (OAI/Combinatorics/Ryser/Construction/Main.lean with its four imports, and OddExtensions.lean) read sorry-free, but I did not run Lean. The companion's solution declaration was not located: its Main.lean is an import-only file in what I read. I found no mathematician's written check. Kalai's blog (7 Oct 2026) describes the Ryser entry and says the results need human verification. The release is credited to 'OpenAI' with no human author; the README attributes most results to 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model' and gives an average of three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; the Ryser entry itself names no system. The preprint PDFs could not be read, so the per-paper AI statement is unverified. (2) Patrick White's arXiv:2609.14281 (13 Sep 2026, single author, v1 only) proves the (r,ν)=(4,2) case, confirming a Tuza 1979 claim that DeBiasio et al. record as unproven. The Methods credit GPT-5.6 Sol with the four-round search that produced the projection lemma (Lemma 2.2) and the proof. They credit Claude (the paper's string is 'Claude (Anthropic, model claude-sonnet-4-20250514)') with 'framing and verification', including building the checker and 'posing each round's scoped target'. I did not record Claude under ai.systems, because its stated role is framing and checking and not the mathematics. The competing reading is that posing each round's target is direction, not checking. No critique or review was found through 13 Oct 2026; VibeMathed records 'Unreviewed'. (3) A Lean repository by Kenta Kitamura (created 3 Oct 2026; Formal Conjectures PR #6812 still open) claims τ ≤ 9 for 4-partite 4-uniform hypergraphs with ν=3. It credits White's lemma for its Lemma 2. A reviewer has not replayed its 232 case obligations and calls the bridge check conditional. Before 2026 the record holds: König (r=2, 1931); Tuza's 1979 (4,2) claim without proof; Tuza's intersecting cases for r=4,5; Aharoni (r=3, 2001); Haxell–Scott (r=4,5, τ ≤ (r−ε)ν, 2012); Francetić et al. (linear intersecting r ≤ 9, 2015/2017); and Haxell–Scott's 2016 lower-bound construction (r−4). Neighbouring 2025-26 papers are recorded as discarded: the Lovász deletion counterexamples (Clow–Haxell–Mohar; Abiad–Garbe–Povill–Spiegel), which disprove a stronger conjecture that would imply Ryser's bound; the Pokrovskiy and Gyárfás–Sárközy bounded-diameter papers, which concern coloured-graph variants; and Hawranick–Luo (2026), a Gyárfás–Király covering result the authors call 'related to a special case'. Keevash et al. (2020) concern Latin squares. Close calls. (a) Whether the OpenAI counterexamples count: the verification status is not established, and the sorry in the challenge files is a placeholder whose solution I read as sorry-free without rebuilding. (b) Whether White's case counts as settling part of the statement: it does settle one (r,ν) instance and is recorded as such. (c) Whether Pokrovskiy's equivalence bears on the hypergraph bound: the paper does not mention hypergraphs; the 2020 survey gives a graph-colouring restatement of Ryser, and I could not read its full text. I took the statement in its standard r-partite form τ ≤ (r−1)ν, because the frozen bullet does not spell out r-partiteness. Two search summaries were wrong and are corrected in the record: a 2024 Haxell–Scott note is actually arXiv:1609.05458 from 2016, and arXiv:2506.21286 is by Abiad, Garbe, Povill and Spiegel, not by Clow, Haxell and Mohar. The Wikipedia article fetched on 13 Oct 2026 does not mention any 2024-2026 result.
competing_reading: Against counting the OpenAI counterexamples as a disproof: they are a company-released batch with no human author, 'different stages of verification', no per-paper AI statement I could read, challenge files that prove their main theorems with sorry, and no rebuilt solution. An error in any construction would leave the bound standing for those ranks. For them: the solution modules read sorry-free, the Lean definitions of the object look faithful (r-partite, intersecting, ν=1, τ=r), and the claimed ranks are large, so they do not contradict any earlier positive result read (r ≤ 5 intersecting; r ≤ 9 linear intersecting). For counting White's (4,2) proof as a settled case: it is a short argument with the author's own account of its checks and an explicit restriction. Against: single author, no referee, the key lemma credited to an AI system on the author's word, and the Lean chain for the ν=2 case does not exist that I found. A reader might also object that the Kitamura ν=3 result depends on White's unreviewed Lemma 2.
what_would_settle_it: For the OpenAI claims: rebuild the lean/OAI modules with Lean and run the comparator configs (including the declaration OAI.Balanced.main_result and the definitions ExplicitFailureAt, BalancedCounterexample and PartiteUniform, none of which I read), and get a written check of at least one construction by a combinatorialist, or an independent Lean replay. For White's (4,2) case: a referee report, an independent check of Lemma 2.2 and the five-sentence proof, or a Lean formalisation of the ν=2 argument. For Kitamura's (4,3): the kernel replay of the 232 case obligations and the pinned four-partite proof that the reviewer asks for, plus a decision on PR #6812. For the Pokrovskiy question: the 2020 survey's exact statement of the graph-colouring form and whether it is equivalent to the hypergraph bound.
